newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain says sector reforms key to promote recovery.
newsitem.headline: Spain says sector reforms key to promote recovery.

text.p: A package of liberalisation measures prepared by Spain's cabinet on Friday holds the key to promoting a recovery and preparing for entry into EMU, Economy Secretary Cristobal Montoro said in an interview on Sunday.
"The plan has two objectives: first to promote a recovery this year and second to prepare the economy in the medium term," Montoro told Spanish daily ABC.
"These reforms will restructure and prepare our productive system for entry and a permanent place in Europe's Monetary Union (EMU)."
Spain's cabinet said on Friday it had prepared a bill which would reform and liberalise key sectors of the economy, extending a series of economic reforms proposed last June.
"As June's plan demonstrated, such measures have good results, in that they are key to securing expectations for lower inflation, an economic recovery and job creation," he said.
Montoro said deregulation and the introduction of more competition in key sectors, would ensure that inflation remained low in the coming years.
"What we are doing with the liberalisation plan is trying to give some sustainability to the economic stabilisation process, to maintain low prices in Spain," he said.
The package will also encourage low interest rates, more investment and thus job creation.
"With lower prices, Spain will be more competitive and interest rates will remain at more accessible levels than previously with a downward tendency this year," he said.
Key sectors to be affected include property, telecommunications, transport, energy and tobacco.
"This is an ambitious programme which will be the government's assignment for 1997 and we expect to approve all the necessary laws during this year," Montoro said.
He added that while some of the more complicated laws would not be ready for approval until the end of the year, others were ready to be approved by the cabinet in the next few weeks.
Yet others had already been approved this year, including an important liberalisation of the telecommunications sector and steps toward decentralising gasoline and diesel distribution.
